excerpts.finding: All three paragraphs were read on physical318–319/printed302–303, including the two-line continuation on319. Sleeping Hermas receives a revelation from a very handsome young man. The Sibyl identification is rejected; the woman is the Church, created first of all, with the world set in order for her sake. The house vision retains not giving the book, words still to add, the woman completing them and disclosure through Hermas to all elect. Two booklets go to Clement and Grapte; Clement sends to outside cities by commission, Grapte admonishes widows/orphans, Hermas reads in this city with presiding elders. Normalized source matches this inspected extent; no body change is made.

All V2iv was read in PlateII physical13. The opening has a question mark near moi and lacks the explicit sleeping participle in its main line. The young man, Sibyl rejection, Church, old-age question, first-created and world-order claims remain. Paragraph2 retains words to add, first-person completion and disclosure through Hermas to all elect. Paragraph3 names both recipients and their tasks, commission, outside cities, widows/orphans and local reading with presiding elders. The admonish verb has bracketed end letters; do not count them as fully unbracketed preserved text. This is the same Athos codex, not another edition vote or fresh original-photo collation.

All explicit8.1–3 ab/app/rdg layers were read; no gap or supplied elements occur. In8.1 first hand lacks I said to him, Why then old? Because he says; S1 adds that exchange. Church, first-created and world-order claims remain. In8.2 first epitelesō is changed by S1 and ca to apotelesō; ca corrects the all-words spelling. Through Hermas and all elect remain. In8.3 ca adds oun and changes Garptē to Graptē; S1 changes the entrusted spelling. Both named recipients and distinct tasks, outside cities, widows/orphans and reading with presiding elders remain. Correctors are not additional codices; original photographs were not collated.

All V2iv was read on physical30–31/printed11–12. Sleeping, young man, Sibyl rejection, Church, first-created and world-made remain. Paragraph2 has the not-yet reply and words to add to Hermas. Printed per te, through you, is explicitly Angero’s conjecture against reported aperto in the codices; it is not preserved Latin agreement. Paragraph3 retains two booklets, Clement/Grapte, outside cities, commission, admonition to widows/orphans, and local reading with presiding elders. Apparatus spelling and other reported forms are distinguished.

All V2iv was read across physical122/124/126, printed25/27/29. Sleeping, Sibyl rejection, Church, first-created and world-created remain. Paragraph2 has church elders, denial of giving the book, words to add and complete, and per te disclosure to elect. Paragraph3 names two books and one to Clement, to send to other cities; it lacks a separately named Grapte recipient and the full Clement commission clause. Widows/orphans receive admonition in a plural formulation, and final reading is with seniors and older church members. Printed27’s suggestion of lost words or translator confusion with Grapte is an editorial hypothesis, not preserved missing words. Printed29 monebunt is edited against reported monebant.

All V2iv was read on physical129/printed117 through the edition’s Latin rendering. Sleeping, young man, rejected Sibyl identification, Church, created before all and world-created remain. In2 the completion clause addresses Hermas, when you finish all the words, against the selected woman’s I complete. Paragraph3 retains two books, Clement and those in outside cities, but no separately named Grapte; teaching widows/orphans from the book and Hermas reading with presiding elders remain. This is mediated versional evidence, not direct Geʿez or a new Latin codex family.
